Re: Mr. Yuxiang Meng , aged 21 years old

I am writing this letter to refer you Mr. Meng, a 21-year-old overseas student , who is presenting with
symptoms and signs suggestive of acute manic episode. Your assessment and management would be
highly appreciated.

It is worth noting that Mr. Meng only speaks basic English and accepted seeing you because you are a
doctor with Chinese background with the ability to speak Mandarin.

Upon Mr. Meng first visit, his examination revealed that he had elevated mood disorder associated with
delusional thoughts. Therefore, he was given diazepam and was referred to a local community mental
health for urgent assessment. One month later, his mental health team stated that he is not considered
dangerous to himself or others and that he is scared of the idea of psych. Moreover, Upon examination, he
is still having delusional thoughts and tangential. However, it is less than before due to well sleeping post
diazepam. Thus, he was commenced to quetiapine, decrease diazepam dose and potassium tablets to be
reviewed four days later.

On today's review, Mr. Meng was settled. Nonetheless, his uncle suspected that he is not compliance to his
medication .In addition, he was noted to have unusual behavior the earlier night .On examination, patient
had an elevation in mood, pressure in speech as well as fixated delusional thoughts and he stripped in
front of the doctor. Therefore, he was given larger doses of his medication but he refused to take them.

If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.
